mcqs.q: The foundation stone of Sri Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple) in Amritsar was laid by which revered Sufi saint?
mcqs.exp: At the invitation of Guru Arjan Dev Ji (5th Sikh Guru), Sufi saint Hazrat Mian Mir laid the foundation stone in December 1588.

mcqs.q: On which auspicious festival in Punjab did General Reginald Dyer order the infamous Jallianwala Bagh massacre on 13 April 1919?
mcqs.exp: Thousands of citizens assembled at Jallianwala Bagh on Baisakhi to peacefully protest the Rowlatt Act.

subtopics.name: Geography
subtopics.summary: Location, borders, physical terrain, and major river systems of Punjab.

facts.title: Capital & Geographic Scope
facts.content: The capital is Chandigarh. Punjab covers a geographic area of 50,362 sq km across 23 administrative districts.

facts.title: Major Rivers & Drainage Systems
facts.content: Key river systems flowing through the region include: Sutlej (Bhakra-Nangal), Beas, Ravi.

facts.title: Geographical Landscape & Highlights
facts.content: Land of the Five Rivers. Cradle of the Sikh faith, Granary of India, pivotal in the Green Revolution. Home to Sri Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple), Jallianwala Bagh, and Wagah Border.

subtopics.name: History & Culture
subtopics.summary: Historical formation, classical/folk dances, and vibrant festivals of Punjab.

facts.title: State Formation & Language
facts.content: Punjab was formally instituted on 1 November 1966. Official language(s): Punjabi.

facts.title: Dance Forms & Traditional Arts
facts.content: Celebrated traditional and folk dance forms: Bhangra, Giddha, Jhumar, Sammi.

facts.title: Major Festivals & Celebrations
facts.content: Prominent cultural festivals: Baisakhi, Lohri, Gurpurab, Hola Mohalla (Anandpur Sahib).

subtopics.name: Government & Polity
subtopics.summary: Constitutional leadership, administrative structure, and state symbols of Punjab.

facts.title: Governor & Constitutional Head
facts.content: The current Governor is Gulab Chand Kataria.

facts.title: Chief Minister & Administration
facts.content: The Chief Minister of Punjab is Bhagwant Mann.

facts.title: High Court Jurisdiction
facts.content: Judicial jurisdiction falls under Punjab and Haryana High Court (Chandigarh).

facts.title: Official State Symbols
facts.content: State Animal: Blackbuck | State Bird: Northern goshawk (Baaz) | State Flower: Gladiolus | State Tree: Sheesham (Tahli).

subtopics.name: Economy & Agriculture
subtopics.summary: Natural resources, minerals, industrial clusters, and agriculture in Punjab.

facts.title: Mineral Wealth & Natural Resources
facts.content: Principal minerals and resources: Silica sand, Quartzite, Gypsum.

facts.title: Economic Profile & Industries
facts.content: Punjab plays a vital role in India's economy through key agricultural production, manufacturing corridors, and services.

subtopics.name: Places, Monuments & Tourism
subtopics.summary: Heritage landmarks, national parks, and tourism attractions in Punjab.

facts.title: Historic Monuments & Cultural Sites
facts.content: Prominent monuments and heritage landmarks: Sri Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple, Amritsar), Jallianwala Bagh, Wagah Border, Qila Mubarak (Bathinda).

facts.title: National Parks & Protected Areas
facts.content: Key protected conservation areas: Harike Wetland (Ramsar Site), Abohar Wildlife Sanctuary.

subtopics.name: State Schemes & Awards
subtopics.summary: Prominent welfare schemes, civic initiatives, and state honors of Punjab.

facts.title: Key State Welfare Schemes
facts.content: Notable welfare initiatives and government programs: Aam Aadmi Clinic, Mukh Mantri Teerth Yatra, Farishtey Scheme.
